message.content:
In Blackjack an Ace is a “flexible” card – it can be worth **either 1 or 11 points**.  
The dealer (or the player) chooses the value that gives the best possible hand, subject to the following rules:

| Situation | How the Ace is counted |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Single Ace** | If counting it as 11 keeps the hand ≤ 21, it is treated as 11. If 11 would bust the hand, it is treated as 1. |
| **Multiple Aces** | One Ace can be counted as 11 while the others are counted as 1. If even that combination would bust, all Aces are counted as 1. |
| **Splitting Aces** | In most casinos, if you’re dealt a pair of Aces you may split them into two hands. After splitting, each Ace is usually counted as 11 (unless you hit a 10‑value card on the split hand, which would then force it to count as 1). |
| **Dealer’s Rules** | The dealer follows a fixed rule: hit on a “soft” 17 (a hand that contains an Ace counted as 11, e.g., Ace‑6) and stand on a “hard” 17 (no Ace counted as 11). |

**Bottom line:** An Ace is worth 11 unless that would cause the hand to exceed 21, in which case it is worth 1. This flexibility is what makes the Ace the most valuable card in Blackjack.
